text: The earth was formless and dark. Then God spoke: “Let there be light!” And light came into the darkness. God saw that the light was good. He separated the light from the darkness, calling the light Day and the darkness Night. There was evening and morning—the first day. From Scripture. God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.

God spoke again. He made a wide, open space between the waters, separating the waters below from the waters above. God called the open space Sky. Above the waters stretched a great expanse. There was evening and morning—the second day. From Scripture. God called the expanse “sky”.

God gathered the waters, and dry land appeared. He called the dry land Earth and the gathered waters Seas. God saw that it was good. Then the land grew green with grass, seed-bearing plants, and trees bearing fruit. God saw that it was good. There was evening and morning—the third day. From Scripture. God called the dry land “earth”, and the gathering together of the waters he called “seas”. God saw that it was good.

God made lights in the sky: the sun to rule the day, the moon to rule the night, and the stars. These lights marked the seasons, days, and years. God set them in the sky to give light to the earth. God saw that it was good. There was evening and morning—the fourth day. From Scripture. God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.

God spoke, and the waters filled with living creatures. Great sea creatures and small swimming things moved through the seas. Birds flew across the sky. God saw that it was good. He blessed the creatures, telling them to multiply and fill the seas and the sky with life. There was evening and morning—the fifth day. From Scripture. God said, “Let the waters abound with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”

God made the land animals: creatures that walked, leaped, and crept along the ground. Then God made people—male and female—in His own image. God blessed them and gave them responsibility to rule and care for His world. He looked at everything He had made. It was very good. There was evening and morning—the sixth day. From Scripture. God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them. God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.

The heavens and the earth were finished, with all their life and beauty. On the seventh day, God rested from His work. God was not tired. His work of creation was complete. He blessed the seventh day and made it holy—a day set apart. His good world was finished. From Scripture. God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.
Come explore the Bible with me! We will learn about God and His Son, Jesus.
Genesis tells us how God made the world. This is where the story that leads to Jesus begins!
We’ll read, play, remember Bible verses, and write. Tap “Open the book” to begin!
You have read how God made the world. Now let us remember it together.
You have seen the good world God made, friend — and remembered how it all began. God made everything, and it was very good.
